attempts.summary: Configured dynamic BGP peering between node1 and node2 (SONiC switches, both preconfigured in AS 65100) over their transit link so each learns the other's private /24 (node3's 192.168.13.0/24 behind node1, node4's 192.168.24.0/24 behind node2) via routing protocol rather than manual routes on the switches. node3 and node4 each keep a single static route pointing at their own gateway switch for the remote /24 (unavoidable single-hop config, not a hand-entered route for the peer's network). Verified end-to-end node3<->node4 reachability. Discovered and fixed a systemd ordering-cycle bug (WantedBy=sonic.target vs bgp.service Requires=sonic.target) that silently dropped our BGP-reapply unit on every SONiC boot; after the fix, BGP session and routes recover fully automatically on reboot with no manual steps. All 4 managed nodes were restarted one at a time (node3, node4, node1 x3 to validate the persistence fix, node2 x1), each with boot_id proof of a genuine restart and post-restart verification of BGP/routes/reachability.
